title: Move profile avatar image processing off the UI thread
goal: Prevent large PhotosPicker images from blocking SwiftUI interactions by decoding and compressing avatar thumbnails away from the main actor.
context: The profile editor currently loads full-resolution photo Data, creates UIImage, resizes with UIGraphicsImageRenderer, and JPEG-encodes inside a Task created by a SwiftUI onChange handler. That Task inherits the main actor from the view, so large source photos can cause visible UI hitches. Keep the current local AppStorage format and 512-pixel avatar presentation.
forbidden_changes: Do not change avatar AppStorage keys or the existing user/Agent avatar separation.
Do not add third-party dependencies or change the profile UI design.
Do not store original full-resolution photos in UserDefaults.
Do not claim physical-device frame-time improvements without device profiling.
acceptance_criteria: Photo decoding, thumbnail generation, and JPEG compression run in a detached background task using ImageIO/CoreGraphics rather than a main-actor UIGraphicsImageRenderer.
Both user and Agent avatar pickers use the same bounded thumbnail processor.
Stored avatar output remains JPEG and has a maximum pixel dimension of 512.
Failed or cancelled processing does not overwrite the previously saved avatar.
Agent Task Contract, M3, and Apple Native Build & Unsigned IPA pass on the final PR head.
verification: Review that no UIKit image rendering or full-resolution UIImage decoding remains in the PhotosPicker processing path.
Confirm all required PR workflows pass on the exact final PR head.
dependencies: UI V2 avatar editor in PR #554
recovery: If ImageIO APIs trigger Swift concurrency or platform compile errors, keep the processing helper nonisolated and return only Sendable Data across the detached-task boundary. Do not fall back to main-thread processing silently.
